name: Walter Pater
bio: Fellow and Tutor of Brasenose College, Oxford (1839-94), and the writer whose Studies in the History of the Renaissance (1873) formed the aesthetic creed of Wilde's generation at Oxford. Its six-page 'Conclusion' caused enough of a stir that Pater removed it from the second edition of 1877. In July of that same year he wrote to Wilde, then twenty-two and unknown, to praise an article and ask to meet him. Wilde copied the letter out in full and posted it to a friend, unable to keep it to himself.
bio_note: His own letter is quoted as the primary source and Wilde's transcription is the manuscript; the editors note Wilde got three small words wrong, which is recorded rather than silently corrected.
